Town Clerk
Town Clerk
Overview
The Town Clerk’s Office is the official record keeper of the Town and serves as a central point of contact between residents and municipal government. Established under MGL Chapter 41, the Town Clerk is responsible for maintaining the Town’s vital records, official documents, bylaws, and meeting records, and for ensuring transparency, accountability, and public access to municipal information.
The office of the Town Clerk is recognized as one of the oldest continuous public service positions in history, with roots that can be traced back to ancient Greece, where record keepers played a critical role in preserving laws and democratic processes.
The Town Clerk serves as the Town’s Chief Election Official, administering all local, state, and federal elections in accordance with Massachusetts election law, including voter registration, early voting, vote-by-mail, the annual town census, and the certification of election results. The office also supports Town Meeting and other public bodies by posting legal notices, attesting official actions, and maintaining permanent records.
In addition, the Town Clerk’s Office administers licenses and permits as required by law, manages public records requests, and provides guidance to boards, committees, and the public on statutory procedures and compliance. Through these responsibilities, the Town Clerk’s Office plays a vital role in preserving the integrity of local government and ensuring the effective operation of the Town.
